title: Model a time slot
prompt: Declare `Slot` so that it holds a `string Day` and an `int Hour`, and so that two slots with the same day and hour are equal with `==`. Give Slot a public constructor accepting day then hour. Write `public static class Slots` with public static methods `bool Clash(Slot a, Slot b)` and `Slot NextHour(Slot slot)`. `Clash(Slot a, Slot b)` returns true when the two slots are the same day and hour. `NextHour(Slot slot)` returns a slot on the same day, one hour later, and leaves the slot it was given unchanged.
hints: Which kind of type compares its values with ==, and which compares references?
A record gives you the constructor, the properties and value equality in one line.
Declare public record Slot(string Day, int Hour);. Clash can compare with ==, and NextHour can use with.
checkLabels: Two slots with the same day and hour must be equal with ==.
Two slots on the same day and hour must clash.
Slots on different days must not clash.
Slots at different hours must not clash.
NextHour must give the same day, one hour later.
NextHour must leave the slot it was given unchanged.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Keeps Slot as a class, so == compares references.
Compares only the day when checking for a clash.

feedback: If two equal-looking slots are not equal with ==, look at how Slot is declared. Then check Clash against a slot that differs in only one value.
